question: In covering a distance of 162 km, Anmol takes 3 hours more than Nikhil. If Anmol doubles his speed, then he would take 6 hours less than Nikhil. Anmol's speed is:
solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

When distance is constant, speed and time are inversely proportional.

As Anmol doubles his speed, his time gets halved. Reduction in time = T − T/2 = T/2.

Total time saved = 3 hours (initially more than Nikhil) + 6 hours (later less than Nikhil) = 9 hours.

⇒ T/2 = 9 hours ⇒ Original Time (T) = 18 hours.

Anmol's speed = Distance ÷ Time = 162 ÷ 18 = 9 km/hr.

**∴ The correct answer is 9 km/hr.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Total distance = 162 km

Anmol takes 3 hours more than Nikhil initially.

If Anmol doubles his speed, he takes 6 hours less than Nikhil.

**Formula Used:**

Speed = Distance ÷ Time
